title: Bet
hookLine: bayit, a house; the letter that opens the Torah

lines: A ROOM WITH THE DOOR OPEN.
cards: "In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth." The Torah's first line, in the old Jewish Publication Society translation. In Hebrew the first word is bereshit, and its first letter isn't alef.
It's bet, the second letter. Before the light, before the waters, there's this one small shape on the parchment: a flat roof, a floor, a wall on the right, and on the left, an opening.
Squint, and it's a room with the door left open. The rabbis squinted.

teach.b: First, the name. Say the letter's name and you're close to bayit, the Hebrew word for house. It's the bet in Beit Knesset, a synagogue, a house of gathering, and in Beit Lechem, Bethlehem, the house of bread.
Second, the shape. The same midrash that gave alef its promise at Sinai asks why the world begins with bet, and answers with the shape.
Bet is closed above, closed below, closed behind, and open only in the direction the line is going. So, the rabbis say, don't ask what is above the heavens, below the depths, or before the beginning.
Start from here and look forward.

Hebrew runs right to left, so bet's open side faces left, toward every word that comes after it. Third, a house. Some readers put the two thoughts together: a world that begins with a house is a world made to be lived in.
Not a monument. A home, with its door facing what comes next.
Fourth, the week just past: thirty days of slowly coming back, a stone and a candle, then the holy tongue, twenty-two letters, right to left, a silent alef, and now a house.
Seven days that walked from the grave into the alphabet, and found, at its second letter, a place to live.

how: Jewish learners meet bet as the second letter, linked to bayit, house; the Torah opens with bereshit, which begins with bet, and a midrash reads the letter's shape, closed on three sides and open on one, as a lesson about where to look.

games.q: you're one of the rabbis, asking why the Torah begins with bet. what does the midrash point to?
o: bet's shape: closed on three sides, open forward.
games.why: the shape. look forward from the beginning, not above, below or before it.

practice: If you're at home, let your eyes move slowly around the room; if not, picture the room you'll sleep in tonight.

Notice what's above you, what's under you, and the door, then rest your attention on the door, the open side, and let a question sit: what might come through it today? If you pray, bring your home into your prayer.

wordCard.voice: Bet. The second letter, close to bayit, house: closed on three sides, open toward what comes next, and the first letter of the Torah. Today's word.
